# A drag proxy hides its content from down() and up(), so getReference goes null

## Context

Promoted from a `defect-note` after a second, independent signal.

1. **Measured** while taking #18763's AC-1 (PR #18774, merged): the Colors grid went `null` from `controller.Component#getReference` **while alive, mounted and rendering**. At the throwing moment its ancestor chain read `dashboard.Panel → DragProxyContainer → dashboard.Container` — a dashboard drag had re-parented the panel into the proxy. Nothing was destroyed; the lookup simply could not see it. The ticket's own premise (a `null` proves a destroy) was falsified by that measurement.
2. **Flagged independently** by @neo-opus-grace reviewing the app-side fix: warming the references at construction leaves a literal widget list in `apps/colors/view/ViewportController.mjs` that duplicates what three call sites already name. *"A fourth widget or a rename loses the protection silently and returns as the same one-in-three CI red."* The workaround is load-bearing precisely because the engine cannot answer the question the app is asking.

## The Problem

The engine has **two** notions of parent, and only one of them survives a drag:

| notion | written by | read by |
|---|---|---|
| `parentId` — structural, the render parent | `DragZone#createDragProxy` sets the proxy's to `proxyParentId` (`'document.body'`); the hosted widget's becomes the proxy's id | `ComponentManager#down` via `childMap` / `getDirectChildren`, and `ComponentManager#up`, which walks `component.parentId` (`src/manager/Component.mjs:634`) |
| `parentComponent` — logical, the owner | `DragZone#createDragProxy` sets it to `me.owner`, the container the drag started in | `component.Abstract#parent`, which prefers it: `me.parentComponent \|\| (me.parentId === 'document.body' ? null : Neo.getComponent(me.parentId))` (`src/component/Abstract.mjs:186`) |

So while a drag is in flight:

- `viewport.down({reference: 'grid'})` → **null**. `down()` descends `childMap`, the panel is no longer a child of the dashboard, and the proxy hangs off `document.body`.
- `ComponentManager.up(grid.id, ...)` → leaves the logical tree at the proxy, because it walks `parentId` too.
- `grid.parent.parent…` → **does** reach the dashboard, because the `parent` getter bridges the proxy.

One of those three is right and the other two are not, and the disagreement is invisible until a controller resolves a reference mid-drag — which is a normal thing for a timer-driven app to do, and produced a ~1-in-3 CI red for a day.

`controller.Component#getReference` is only the first victim: its cache is a hint and its fallback is `me.component.down({reference: name})`, so any consumer of `down()` / `up()` has the same blind spot. #18763 explicitly put `getReference` out of scope, which is why this is filed separately rather than folded in.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/manager/Component.mjs:112` `down()` — matches the component, then recurses through `getDirectChildren(parentId)`; `:618` `up()` — `while (component?.parentId)`.
- `src/component/Abstract.mjs:183` `get parent()` — the only logical-aware traversal in the trio.
- `src/draggable/DragZone.mjs:315` — `isContainer` proxies get `config.parentComponent = me.owner` and `parentId: me.proxyParentId`; `src/draggable/dashboard/SortZone.mjs#startRemoteDrag` creates the proxy with the live widget as its item.
- `src/draggable/DragProxyContainer.mjs#destroy` — `items = []` first, so the hosted widget survives the proxy. Object permanence is intended and is honoured; only the lookup disagrees.
- `src/controller/Component.mjs:113` — the existing `getReference` TODO covers a *different* failure (remove-then-add with the same key, returning a stale component). This one returns nothing rather than the wrong thing.

## The Fix

Make the two manager traversals agree with the `parent` getter about who a component's parent is, rather than teaching each caller to compensate:

- `up()` — walk `component.parent` instead of `parentId`, so a logical owner set by a drag proxy is followed.
- `down()` — when descending, include components whose `parentComponent` is the current node, not only the `childMap` entries. The proxy's own subtree then hangs where its owner is.

Both are one-place changes with engine-wide reach, which is why this needs measurement before code: `childMap` is the O(1) optimisation `getDirectChildren` exists for, and a naive union walk risks a component being visited twice (proxy hosted AND child-mapped) or an infinite walk if a `parentComponent` cycle is possible.

**The deletion that pays for it** (`§self_evolving_systems` accretion defense): `apps/colors/view/ViewportController.mjs` loses its warm-the-references line and its literal widget list — the workaround this ticket makes unnecessary — which is also @neo-opus-grace's drift note discharged rather than papered over.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — a unit arm builds a real container tree, hosts a subtree in a real `DragProxyContainer` (`parentId: 'document.body'`, `parentComponent: owner`), and asserts that `down()` from the owner finds a component inside the proxy, and `up()` from that component reaches the owner. Red-first against `dev`. `test/playwright/unit/apps/colors/ViewportController.spec.mjs` has the hosting recipe.
- [ ] **AC-2** — a component reachable through both paths (child-mapped AND proxy-hosted) is returned once, not twice, by `down(..., false)`.
- [ ] **AC-3** — the traversal cost is measured, not assumed: the `childMap` fast path stays the fast path, with a number for a tree of realistic depth before and after.
- [ ] **AC-4** — `apps/colors/view/ViewportController.mjs` drops the construction-time warm list, and `tearOutMatrix.spec.mjs` runs clean ×10 consecutively without it. That is the proof the engine now answers what the app was working around.
- [ ] **AC-5** — the dashboard and draggable component suites stay green, and the Workstation tour arms are run as the widest consumer of `down()`.

## Out of Scope

- The `getReference` cache and its `:113` TODO (remove-then-add staleness) — a different failure mode; #18763's Architectural Reality enumerates the cache's mutation sites.
- Changing what a drag proxy does. `parentId` / `parentComponent` as written are deliberate and the proxy is the reason the widget keeps rendering; this leaf changes the readers, not the writer.
- Multi-window re-parenting (`startRemoteDrag`'s `appName` handover) beyond what AC-1's arm needs.

## Avoided Traps

- **Fixing it in `getReference`.** The controller is one caller; `down()` and `up()` are engine surfaces with many. A guard there would leave the next consumer to rediscover this.
- **Another app-side warm list.** That is the workaround this ticket exists to delete; adding a second copy elsewhere would make the engine gap permanently invisible.
- **Assuming a `null` means destroyed.** #18763's body inferred exactly that, and the instrumented run falsified it. Anything here that reasons from a `null` needs the same instrumentation.
- **Skipping the cost measurement.** `getDirectChildren`'s docblock names the `childMap` as the optimisation that avoids iterating the registry; a union walk that quietly reintroduces the iteration would trade a correctness bug for a performance one.

- #18763 / PR #18774 — where this was measured; its Deltas section carries the falsification.

- 2026-09-16T11:43:47Z @tobiu referenced in commit `7710767` - "fix(manager): both traversals agree with `parent` about who a component's parent is (#18781)

`component.Abstract#parent` ranks the owner over the render parent: `parentComponent` first,
`parentId` second. `ComponentManager#down()` and `#up()` knew only the second, and a drag is
where the two disagree — `draggable.DragProxyContainer` roots the dragged component at
`document.body` and keeps the container it came from as `parentComponent`. For as long as the
drag lasts, a live, mounted, rendering component was invisible to a lookup from its own owner,
which is what made `controller.Component#getReference` answer null mid-drag and take the Colors
grid down with it.

`up()` now walks `parent`, and `down()` descends through `getOwnedChildren()`: the render
children, plus whatever a proxy holds for this component, each returned once. `ownerMap` is the
same reverse index shape as `childMap`, maintained at the same three seams, and
`getDirectChildren()` is untouched — `mixin.VdomLifecycle` unmounts by it, so the render question
keeps its own answer.

What this deletes is the point: `apps/colors/view/ViewportController.mjs` loses the
resolve-early workaround #18763 needed, and its arms now witness the engine answering instead.

Cost, measured on a 853-component tree, 200 full non-matching walks, three samples per head:
with an empty `ownerMap` 0.491 ms against dev's 0.484 ms; with one entry — any app holding a
menu — 0.635 ms against 0.489 ms. The size check keeps the first case at one Map read per node;
the second pays a second read, on a path whose 22 call sites are all lookups rather than frames."
- 2026-09-16T12:38:53Z @tobiu referenced in commit `856e667` - "fix(manager): the ownership walk visits each component once, however many keys hold it (#18781)

A component can sit in both reverse indexes under DIFFERENT keys. `menu.List` renders an open
submenu under the app's main view and keeps the component that opened it as `parentComponent`,
so a walk from the main view met the submenu once through each index — `getOwnedChildren()`
only deduped against the node it was expanding. `down()` now normalises its selector once and
hands the recursion to `walkDown()`, which remembers what it has visited for the whole walk.

Only a component with an owner can be reached twice, and only an owner link can close a cycle,
so only those are remembered. The first version remembered every node and cost +74 % on a full
walk; guarding owned components alone is +46 % with one owned component in the app and nothing
measurable without one. `up()` carries the same visited set, so a `parentComponent` cycle ends
both walks.

The JSDoc on `ownerMap`, `getOwnedChildren()` and `down()` now describes the population this
changes — button menus, submenus, the tab overflow control and Markdown-injected components for
their whole life, a drag proxy's content for the length of the drag — instead of the drag alone.

`getOwnedChildren()` and `removeFromIndex()` move to their alphabetical slots; the delta reads
cleanly with `--color-moved`."
